blocks.intro: Most disposal calls are one of these:

tiles.body: Something is jammed in the grinding chamber. Turn it off at the switch and keep your hands out.
Try the reset button on the bottom. If it still won't run, the motor or wiring has failed.
A leak at the flange or a hose is a repair. A leak from the unit's body means replacement.
Food buildup in the disposal or the drain below it. See [drain cleaning](/arlington-heights/drain-cleaning) if it backs up.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposals in Arlington Heights Kitchens
blocks.intro: Kitchens here range from original postwar layouts to recent remodels, and disposal work varies with them.

items.h3: Adding a Disposal to an Older Kitchen
items.body: Some kitchens from the 1950s and 1960s never had one. We check the drain size, the dishwasher hookup and whether there's power under the sink before quoting.

items.h3: Older Drain Lines Under the Sink
items.body: A new disposal can expose a weak, corroded drain arm in an older home. We check it while we're there so the sink drains properly.
In homes from the 1970s and 1980s, a disposal swap is usually straightforward. We match the mount when we can to keep the job quick.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: A disposal job should be quick and clean.

steps.body: Jam, leak, tripped reset or a dead motor. We find out which and show you.
Repair or replace, you get one number before we start.
We run the disposal and the dishwasher and check every connection for drips.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposal Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Should I repair or replace my garbage disposal?
items.preview: A jam or loose connection is a repair. A leaking body or dead motor means replace.
items.answer: A jam, a tripped reset or a loose connection can be fixed. A disposal leaking from its body or with a burned-out motor needs replacing. We'll tell you which.

items.q: What shouldn't go down a disposal?
items.preview: Grease, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
items.answer: Grease and oil, bones, fibrous scraps like celery and corn husks, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta. They jam the unit or build up in the drain line.

items.q: How long do garbage disposals last?
items.preview: Often 8 to 15 years, depending on the model and use.
items.answer: Many last around 8 to 15 years. Frequent jams, leaks and louder grinding mean it's near the end.

items.preview: Food trapped under the splash guard and in the drain.
items.answer: Food gets trapped under the rubber splash guard and in the drain below. Run cold water for 15 to 20 seconds after each use and grind a few ice cubes now and then. A smell that keeps returning usually means the drain line needs cleaning.

items.q: How much does garbage disposal replacement cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the unit and any plumbing or electrical work. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit and whether plumbing or electrical changes are needed. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
